questions.q: In a slow stage's task Summary Metrics, which pattern does Databricks describe as a sign of skew?

options.t: All task durations are nearly the same
options.why: Even durations mean no skew.

options.t: Max task duration is 50% or more above the 75th percentile
The median task duration is longer than one minute in every stage of the job
options.why: Long tasks alone aren't skew; skew is an uneven distribution.

options.t: The number of tasks equals the number of cores
options.why: That is about parallelism, not skew.

questions.explain: In Summary Metrics, compare Max duration to the 75th percentile: 50% or more above it suggests skew.

questions.q: Where does a stage show that it spilled to disk?

options.t: In the cluster's event log, as a SPILL event logged for each affected executor
options.why: Spill shows as statistics in the stage details.

options.t: In DESCRIBE HISTORY of the table being written
options.why: History lists table operations, not spill.

options.t: In the stage details at the top of the stage page, as spill statistics
In system.billing.usage for the job
options.why: Billing usage records consumption, not spill.

questions.explain: The stage details at the top of the stage page show spill statistics when the stage has spill; none shown means no spill.

questions.q: What is spill?

options.t: Rows that fail an expectation and are dropped
options.why: Spill is about memory, not data quality.

options.t: Data written to disk when execution memory runs out
Files that a failed write left behind in the table directory before VACUUM ran
options.why: Those are uncommitted files, removed by VACUUM.

options.t: A broadcast table too big for the driver
options.why: Spill is execution memory exhausted in tasks.

questions.explain: Spill happens when Spark runs low on execution memory (used for shuffles, joins, sorts and aggregations) and writes data from memory to disk; it is most common in shuffles.

questions.q: Which remedies does Databricks list for a stage that spills?

options.t: Set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to auto
Use instances with more memory
Set the broadcast threshold to -1
options.why: That disables broadcasting; it isn't a spill remedy.

options.t: Disable Photon
options.why: Disabling Photon isn't a documented spill remedy.

options.t: Add more Run if conditions to the job
options.why: Job conditions don't affect memory use in a stage.

questions.explain: For spill: shuffle.partitions=auto, process fewer rows or columns, more executor memory, fewer larger workers for complex joins, smaller streaming batches.

questions.q: Which kinds of skew can adaptive query execution split automatically?

options.t: Skewed partitions in sort-merge and shuffle-hash joins
Skew in any groupBy aggregation, by splitting the hot key's partition in two
options.why: AQE's skew handling applies to joins, not aggregations.

options.t: Skew in broadcast joins
options.why: Broadcast joins are never skew-optimised.

options.t: Skewed files in a Delta table on disk
options.why: AQE works at query run time, not on stored files.

questions.explain: AQE splits skewed partitions in sort-merge and shuffle-hash joins; broadcast joins are never skew-optimised, and aggregations aren't covered.

questions.q: A stored Delta table is skewed on the column most queries filter by. Which documented fix applies to the table itself?

options.t: Salting every query's filter on that column
options.why: Salting fixes skewed aggregations at query time; for a stored table, liquid clustering is listed.

options.t: Raising spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold
options.why: That changes join strategy, not the table's layout.

options.t: Running VACUUM with a shorter retention
options.why: VACUUM removes old files; it doesn't fix skew.

options.t: Liquid clustering on that column

questions.explain: Fixes for skew include liquid clustering for a skewed stored table; liquid clustering suits skewed data and high-cardinality filter columns.

questions.q: A table receives many small appends and queries have slowed. Which command compacts its small files?

options.t: VACUUM
options.why: VACUUM deletes unreferenced old files; OPTIMIZE compacts.

options.t: OPTIMIZE
RESTORE
options.why: RESTORE returns to an earlier version.

options.t: ANALYZE TABLE
options.why: ANALYZE computes statistics.

questions.explain: OPTIMIZE rewrites small files into fewer, larger ones (bin-packing); it is idempotent and makes no data change.

questions.q: What does predictive optimization do on Unity Catalog managed tables?

options.t: Rewrites queries to use better join strategies
options.why: That is AQE; predictive optimization maintains tables.

options.t: Predicts which jobs will fail and retries them early on larger compute
options.why: It maintains tables, not jobs.

options.t: Runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE automatically where they help
Converts external tables to managed tables
options.why: That is ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED.

questions.explain: Predictive optimization automatically runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE on Unity Catalog managed tables, deciding which tables benefit.

questions.q: Predictive optimization is on, and a team also runs OPTIMIZE ... ZORDER BY on a schedule. What should they know?

options.t: Predictive optimization runs Z-order for them on a better schedule, so their own job is redundant
options.why: Predictive optimization never runs ZORDER.

options.t: Predictive optimization never runs Z-order; Databricks recommends liquid clustering instead
Z-order is required for predictive optimization to work
options.why: It isn't; predictive optimization ignores Z-ordered files.

options.t: The two can't be enabled on the same workspace
options.why: They can; predictive optimization just never runs ZORDER.

questions.explain: Predictive optimization's OPTIMIZE never runs ZORDER and ignores Z-ordered files; Databricks recommends liquid clustering instead of partitioning or Z-order.

questions.q: Queries filter on a column that is the 40th column of a wide table, and data skipping doesn't help. Why?

options.t: Data skipping only works on partition columns
options.why: Skipping uses per-file statistics, by default on the first 32 columns.

options.t: Statistics are collected on the first 32 columns by default
Data skipping is switched off on wide tables
options.why: It works; statistics just cover the first 32 columns by default.

options.t: Only columns listed in ZORDER BY get file statistics, and this one never was
options.why: Statistics are collected on write for the first 32 columns.

questions.explain: Statistics are collected automatically on the first 32 columns by default (delta.dataSkippingNumIndexedCols, or delta.dataSkippingStatsColumns).

questions.q: A job ran in 20 minutes for weeks and now takes 70. Where do you compare runs against that baseline?

options.t: In the job's run history and matrix view
In the table's DESCRIBE DETAIL output
options.why: That describes the table, not run durations.

options.t: In the cluster's init script logs
options.why: Run durations are in the job's run history.

options.t: In the notebook's revision history, which records each run's duration
options.why: That tracks code edits, not run durations.

questions.explain: The Jobs UI gives run history and the matrix view, task run details, duration thresholds and notifications; the system.lakeflow tables record runs across the account.

options.t: system.access.audit and system.access.table_lineage, joined on the job ID

options.t: system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline and job_task_run_timeline
system.compute.warehouses
options.why: That describes warehouses.

questions.explain: system.lakeflow has jobs, job_tasks, job_run_timeline, job_task_run_timeline, pipelines and pipeline_update_timeline.

questions.q: Which system table holds all billable usage, in DBUs?

system.query.history

questions.explain: system.billing.usage holds all billable usage, in DBUs, with records usually within 12 hours; join with list prices to get cost.

questions.q: How long does it usually take for usage to appear in system.billing.usage?

options.t: Within one second

At the end of each month

questions.q: How do you query a declarative pipeline's event log?

options.t: DESCRIBE HISTORY on the pipeline's name
options.why: History is for tables; the event log uses event_log().

options.t: SELECT * FROM system.billing.usage WHERE pipeline = ...
options.why: Billing usage holds DBUs, not pipeline events.

options.t: SELECT * FROM event_log(<pipeline id>)
By reading the pipeline's checkpoint files
options.why: Use the event_log() function.

questions.explain: Every pipeline writes an event log (audit, data quality, progress, lineage); query it with SELECT * FROM event_log(<pipelineId>). Don't delete it.

questions.q: A SQL warehouse query is slow. Which tool shows its operators with time, rows and memory each?

options.t: The query profile, opened from query history
The table's DESCRIBE DETAIL
options.why: That describes the table, not the query's execution.

options.t: The job's matrix view
options.why: That shows job runs, not query operators.

options.t: The Git folder's commit log, which records each query's runtime

questions.q: A query's profile says 'Query profile is not available'. What is a likely reason?

options.t: The query failed with a syntax error before planning
options.why: The documented case is a result served from the query cache.

options.t: The results came from the query cache
The warehouse is serverless
options.why: Serverless warehouses have query profiles.

options.t: The table has liquid clustering
options.why: Table layout doesn't remove profiles.

questions.explain: No profile is available for queries served from the query cache; make a trivial change, such as to the LIMIT, to bypass it.

questions.q: A first cluster in a new VNet-injected workspace never responds, and the event log says the compute plane network is misconfigured. What is the likely cause?

options.t: The cluster's runtime version is too old for a workspace created this year
options.why: The message points at routing or a firewall.

options.t: Routing or a firewall stops nodes reaching the control plane
The workspace has no Unity Catalog metastore
options.why: That wouldn't stop nodes bootstrapping.

options.t: The job's timeout was set too low
options.why: This is a compute bootstrap failure, not a job timeout.

questions.explain: 'The compute plane network is misconfigured ... Node daemon ping timeout' means routing or the firewall is incorrect: test connectivity from a VM in the workspace subnet.

questions.q: A cluster's event log shows METASTORE_DOWN events. What does the troubleshooting guide suggest checking?

options.t: Whether a web application firewall or proxy sits in the path
Whether the cluster has enough workers
options.why: The guide points to a WAF or proxy in the path.

options.t: Whether VACUUM ran on the metastore
options.why: The guide points to a WAF or proxy in the path.

options.t: Whether the job that started the cluster has a retry policy configured
options.why: The guide points to a WAF or proxy in the path.

questions.q: A stream failed out of memory on an oversized micro-batch. It restarts and fails again on the same batch. What does the documentation suggest?

options.t: Delete the checkpoint so that the oversized micro-batch is skipped
options.why: That reprocesses everything; the guidance is to scale up compute.

options.t: Lower the watermark to drop the batch
options.why: The planned batch runs again; scale up compute to get past it.

options.t: Switch the output mode to complete
options.why: That doesn't shrink the planned batch.

options.t: Scale up the compute to process the micro-batch

questions.explain: On restart, the micro-batch planned in the previous run is processed again; after an out-of-memory failure you might need to scale up the compute to process it.

questions.q: Where does Databricks recommend installing libraries from, on DBR 13.3 LTS and above with Unity Catalog?

options.t: From DBFS, which any workspace user can update
options.why: DBFS libraries are writable by any user and discouraged.

options.t: From Unity Catalog volumes, on standard-access compute
From an init script that runs pip install on each node

options.t: From the driver's local disk, copied by hand

questions.q: Before adding a library to a cluster, what should you check first to avoid conflicts?

options.t: Whether the library is in the table's lineage graph
options.why: Lineage tracks data, not libraries.

options.t: Whether the runtime already includes it, in the release notes
Whether the cluster has deletion vectors enabled
options.why: That is a table feature, not related to libraries.

options.t: Whether the job has a file arrival trigger
options.why: Triggers don't affect libraries.

questions.explain: Each runtime comes with many libraries; check its release notes before adding anything, and prefer the versions packaged in the runtime.

A notebook that runs shell commands at the start of every job

options.t: Installing libraries through the init script with pinned versions
options.why: Databricks says not to install libraries through init scripts.

options.why: Init scripts are for classic compute.

questions.q: Code must react to a specific Databricks error. What should it check?

options.t: The text of the error message
options.why: Message text may change between releases; use the condition or SQLSTATE.

options.t: The error condition or SQLSTATE
The line number in the stack trace

questions.q: A stream writing a Delta table fails with DELTA_CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION. What does the error point to?

options.t: Several streams are using the same checkpoint to write the table
The table's schema changed since the stream started
options.why: That gives a schema-change error.

options.t: A file in the log was deleted by VACUUM
options.why: That gives DELTA_FILE_NOT_FOUND_DETAILED.

options.t: The source sent duplicate keys to a MERGE
options.why: That gives a multiple-source-row error.

questions.explain: DELTA_CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION occurs when multiple streaming queries use the same checkpoint to write into the table.

questions.q: A lagging stream fails with DELTA_FILE_NOT_FOUND_DETAILED after someone vacuumed its source with a very short retention. What is the fix the error suggests?

options.t: Run RESTORE on the source to bring the files back
options.why: RESTORE can't bring back vacuumed files.

options.t: Increase the stream's trigger interval
options.why: The files are gone; the message suggests a new checkpoint.

options.t: Restart the query with a new checkpoint location
Set the table to append-only
options.why: That doesn't recover the missing files.

questions.explain: DELTA_FILE_NOT_FOUND_DETAILED: a file referenced in the log can't be found, from manual deletion or a VACUUM with too short a retention; restart with a new checkpoint location.

questions.q: A MERGE fails with DELTA_MULTIPLE_SOURCE_ROW_MATCHING_TARGET_ROW_IN_MERGE. What is the fix?

options.t: Retry the MERGE until it succeeds
options.why: The source has duplicate keys; retries fail the same way.

options.t: Switch to Serializable isolation
options.why: Isolation concerns concurrent writers, not duplicate source rows.

options.t: Enable deletion vectors on the target
options.why: That speeds DML; it doesn't fix duplicate matches.

options.t: Deduplicate the source so one row matches each target row

questions.explain: Several source rows matched one target row; preprocess the source to remove duplicates.

questions.q: VACUUM ... RETAIN 1 HOURS fails with DELTA_VACUUM_RETENTION_PERIOD_TOO_SHORT. Why does this safety check exist?

options.t: Writes still in progress could have their files deleted, corrupting the table
VACUUM can only run once a week
options.why: The check protects in-progress writes, not a schedule.

options.t: One hour is below the log retention
options.why: The check is about the deleted-file retention and in-progress writes.

options.t: Retention must be a whole number of days
options.why: The check is about safety, not units.

questions.explain: The retention is too low and may corrupt the table if writes are in progress; Databricks strongly recommends at least 7 days.

questions.q: Why does Databricks recommend liquid clustering for new tables?

options.t: It is the only layout predictive optimization can read
options.why: The reasons are about flexibility and skipping, not readability.

options.t: Its keys can change without rewriting existing data
It removes the need for statistics on any column
options.why: Clustering keys need statistics.

options.t: It makes tables readable by any older client
options.why: It raises the table protocol, so older clients can't read it.

questions.explain: Liquid clustering replaces partitioning and ZORDER; clustering keys can be changed without rewriting existing data, and it suits high-cardinality filters, skew and changing access patterns.
